# README

## Open Food Facts Product Lookup

### What it does

This **free** actor looks up food and grocery products by **barcode (EAN-13 / UPC)** using the open **Open Food Facts** database.
For each barcode you get the product name, brand, quantity, categories, **Nutri-Score**, **NOVA** processing group, **Eco-Score**, ingredients, allergens and per-100g nutrition facts (énergie, matières grasses, sucres, sel, protéines). Ideal for enriching product catalogues, diet apps and food-data pipelines. You only pay your Apify platform usage — the actor itself is free.

### Input

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `barcodes` | array of strings | Product barcodes to look up. One dataset item per barcode. |
| `country` | string | Open Food Facts subdomain: `world` (default), `fr`, `us`, … |

### Output

One item per barcode:

```json
{
  "barcode": "3017620422003",
  "status": "found",
  "product_name": "Nutella",
  "brands": "Ferrero",
  "nutriscore_grade": "e",
  "nova_group": 4,
  "ecoscore_grade": "d",
  "ingredients_text": "Sugar, palm oil, hazelnuts 13%, ...",
  "nutrition": { "energy-kcal_100g": 539, "sugars_100g": 56.3, "salt_100g": 0.107 },
"url": "https://world.openfoodfacts.org/product/3017620422003"
}
```

`status` is `found`, `not_found` or `error`.

### Use cases

- Enrich e-commerce or retail catalogues with nutrition and Nutri-Score data.
- Power diet, nutrition and allergen-checking apps.
- Batch-audit a product list for NOVA / Eco-Score.
- Academic and open-data food research.

### Limitations & fair use

Data comes from the collaborative Open Food Facts project (Open Database License). Coverage and freshness depend on community contributions; some barcodes return `not_found`. A short delay is applied between requests to respect the API.

### More actors by this developer

See more open-data actors on the author profile: https://apify.com/vigilant\_jasmine

Open Food Facts country subdomain to query (e.g. 'world', 'fr', 'us').

# Open Food Facts API

Canonical URL: https://freeapihub.com/apis/open-food-facts-api

- **Category:** Food & Drink
- **Access:** Free
- **Auth:** No Auth
- **Format:** REST
- **Base URL:** https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v2
- **HTTPS:** Yes
- **CORS:** Yes
- **Documentation:** https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/
- **Website:** https://openfoodfacts.org

## Overview

## What is the Open Food Facts API?

Open Food Facts is a **free, open database of food products** from around the world, built by a community much like Wikipedia. Its API lets you look up a product by **barcode** and get its **ingredients, nutrition facts, Nutri-Score, allergens, labels, categories and images**, or search the database by name and attributes. It is used in diet and nutrition apps, scanners, shopping tools and research, and the data is openly licensed for reuse.

## Authentication & setup

There is **no API key** and no signup for reading data. The base URL is `https://world.
openfoodfacts.org/api/v2`, and the core call is `/product/{barcode}.json`, which returns everything known about that product. A search endpoint lets you query by name, category, brand and nutritional attributes. The project asks clients to send a **descriptive User-Agent** identifying your app, so it can contact you if needed.

## What it returns

A product response is detailed: the `product_name`, brands, quantity, a parsed **ingredients** list, a **nutriments** object with values per 100 g and per serving, the **Nutri-Score** and NOVA processing group, allergens and traces, labels (organic, vegan and so on), packaging, categories and image URLs. Because the data is crowdsourced, completeness varies by product, so check whether a field is present before relying on it. The same response also carries the product images at several sizes, which you can show directly in a scanner or a product card.

## Rate limits & pricing
The API is **free with no rate limiting** for reasonable use, and the data is released under an open licence (ODbL), so you can reuse it with attribution. As a community project running on donations, the considerate approach is to **cache** products you look up and avoid heavy bulk scraping through the live API — for large analyses, the project also publishes full data exports you can download.

## Best practices

Send a clear **User-Agent**, request only the fields you need (the API supports field selection to shrink responses), and cache product data by barcode since it changes slowly. Handle missing fields gracefully given the crowdsourced data, attribute Open Food Facts per the licence, and use the bulk exports rather than the live API for analytics. If your app can, encourage users to contribute corrections back to the database. That community contribution is what keeps the dataset growing and improving over time.

## How it compares
Open Food Facts is the leading **open** food-product database, comparable in spirit to other crowdsourced datasets. Commercial nutrition APIs may offer cleaner, guaranteed data behind a paywall; Open Food Facts trades some consistency for open access, global coverage and no cost. For barcode scanning, ingredient and nutrition lookups, and any project that values open data, it is a natural fit.

## Common errors & troubleshooting

A response with `status: 0` means the barcode is not in the database yet — a chance to prompt the user to add it. Missing fields are normal for sparsely documented products, so code defensively. If requests are blocked or throttled, confirm you are sending a descriptive User-Agent and not hammering the live API; switch to the data exports for bulk work.

## Endpoints

### GET /product/{barcode}.json

Get a food product by barcode


| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| barcode | string | Yes | Product barcode (EAN/UPC) |
| fields | string | No | Comma-separated fields to return |

### GET /search

Search products by name and attributes


| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| categories_tags | string | No | Category filter |
| fields | string | No | Fields to return |

## Pros & Cons

- ✅ Free, open database of food products worldwide
- ✅ Barcode lookup for ingredients, nutrition and Nutri-Score
- ✅ No API key; openly licensed data (ODbL)
- ✅ Bulk exports available for heavy analysis
- ⚠️ Crowdsourced data, so completeness varies by product
- ⚠️ Requires a descriptive User-Agent
- ⚠️ Not every barcode is in the database
- ⚠️ Attribution required under the open licence


## FAQ

**Is the Open Food Facts API free?**

Yes, free with no API key and no rate limiting for reasonable use; the data is open under the ODbL licence.

**How do I look up a product?**

Call /product/{barcode}.json to get everything known about it.

excerpts:
# Barcode Lookup API — GTIN/EAN/UPC/ISBN to product data (title, brand, images, nutrition, retailer offers) via Open Food Facts and UPCitemdb, with check-digit validation

> Barcode → one merged product: title/brand/category/image/description + dimensions/model + PACKAGE WEIGHT as an explicit {weight, weight_unit} pair (plus weight_grams, weight_type, weight_source and a weight_confidence flag) + retailer offers&prices (UPCitemdb) + net content + nutrition/ingredients/allergens if food (OFF). Includes check-digit validation, GTIN-13 normalization and issuing-country. source=auto merges both. Weight is published by roughly 1 barcode in 5 (1 in 3 with deep_weight=true) — when no source states one, weight is null, never 0 and never borrowed from a similar product.
> ReefAPI engine `barcode` · 7 endpoints · clean JSON, no scraping or browsers to manage.

## How to call
- **Endpoint:** `POST https://api.reefapi.com/barcode/v1/<action>` with a JSON body.
- **Auth:** header `x-api-key: <YOUR_REEFAPI_KEY>` — create one free (1,000 credits, no card): https://reefapi.com/signup
- **Response (every call):** `{ ok: boolean, data: ..., meta: { record_count, credits, ... }, error: { code, message } }` — branch on `ok`. Failed or blocked calls are free.
- **One key + one shared credit pool** across every ReefAPI API. Per-call credits are listed on each endpoint below.
- **Use it from an AI agent (MCP):** connect `https://api.reefapi.com/mcp` (remote streamable-http, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`) and your assistant can call these actions directly.

## Endpoints

### POST /barcode/v1/lookup — 1 credit
Barcode → one merged product: title/brand/category/image/description + dimensions/model + PACKAGE WEIGHT as an explicit {weight, weight_unit} pair (plus weight_grams, weight_type, weight_source and a weight_confidence flag) + retailer offers&prices (UPCitemdb) + net content + nutrition/ingredients/allergens if food (OFF).
Includes check-digit validation, GTIN-13 normalization and issuing-country. source=auto merges both. Weight is published by roughly 1 barcode in 5 (1 in 3 with deep_weight=true) — when no source states one, weight is null, never 0 and never borrowed from a similar product.

**Parameters:**
- `barcode` (string, required) — The barcode to look up: UPC-A (12), EAN-13 (13), EAN-8 (8), GTIN-14, or ISBN-13 (978/979…). Spaces/dashes are stripped; check digit is validated (mod-10). Aliases: upc, ean, gtin, isbn, code.
- `source` (enum, optional, default "auto") — Which open source(s) to query for lookup/batch. 'auto' merges both. [one of: auto, off, upcitemdb]
- `off_db` (enum, optional, default "food") — Which Open-*-Facts sibling DB to search/lookup against when source=off. lookup auto-falls-back food→products when source=auto. [one of: food, beauty, petfood, products]
- `deep_weight` (boolean, optional, default false) — Spend ONE extra upstream call, per barcode, to chase a weight the product page did not publish. Measured on 61 retailer-sourced barcodes: weight coverage 19.7% off (default, 1 call) → 29.5% on (2 calls). Off by default so the cheap path stays one call. Read weight_confidence before trusting the value either way.

**Returns:** product{barcode, gtin13, gtin_type, valid_check_digit, issuing_country, title, brand, category, description, image, images[], weight, weight_unit (g|kg|oz|lb), weight_grams, weight_type (package|net_content), weight_source, weight_raw, weight_confidence (medium|low|null), weight_flags[], net_content{value, unit, grams, is_volume}, nutrition{} (if food), ingredients, allergens[], offers[] (merchant/price), price_lowest/highest, sources[], field_source{}}

**Example request body:**
```json
{
  "barcode": "5449000000996"
}
```

### POST /barcode/v1/batch — 1 credit

...

5% on (2 calls). Off by default so the cheap path stays one call. Read weight_confidence before trusting the value either way.

**Returns:** products[] (one per input barcode: found bool + merged product with the same weight/weight_unit block as lookup, or not-found), requested, found_count, weight_found_count

**Example request body:**
```json
{
  "barcodes": "5449000000996,0885909950805"
}
```

### POST /barcode/v1/search — 1 credit
Free-text product-name search across the open databases → product cards with pagination. Optional category scope. (Competitor: keyword/title/category search.)

**Parameters:**
- `query` (string, required) — Free-text product-name keyword search (matches title across the open databases). Aliases: q, search, name, title.
- `category` (string, optional) — Optional Open-Food-Facts category tag to scope a search/brand query (e.g. 'sodas', 'chocolate-spreads', 'biscuits').

...

```json
{
  "brand": "coca-cola"
}
```

### POST /barcode/v1/by_prefix — 1 credit
GS1 company-prefix (partial-barcode) search → products whose barcode starts with the given 6+ digits, plus the decoded issuing country. (Competitor: `491234*` partial method.)

**Parameters:**
- `prefix` (string, required) — A GS1 company prefix — the first 6+ digits of a barcode (the competitor's `491234*` partial-barcode method). Returns products whose barcode starts with these digits + the decoded issuing country.
- `off_db` (enum, optional, default "food") — Which Open-*-Facts sibling DB to search/lookup against when source=off. lookup auto-falls-back food→products when source=auto. [one of: food, beauty, petfood, products]
- `page` (integer, optional, default 1) — 1-based page number (clamped 1-1000). Page forward with meta.next_page. Note: Open Food Facts throttles deep pages per-IP; the engine retries on a fresh proxy.

...

- `page_size` (integer, optional, default 20) — Results per page (1-50, default 20); out-of-range values are clamped.

**Returns:** products[] (exact-mpn first, each w/ matched_mpn + exact_match bool), mpn, exact_match_count, count, page, page_count, has_more, next_page

### POST /barcode/v1/validate — 0 credits
Validate + decode a barcode WITHOUT a network call: mod-10 check digit, GTIN type, GTIN-13 normalization, GS1 issuing country, ISBN/Bookland detection. (We EXCEED the competitor here — it has no standalone validate.)

**Parameters:**
- `barcode` (string, required) — The barcode to look up: UPC-A (12), EAN-13 (13), EAN-8 (8), GTIN-14, or ISBN-13 (978/979…).
Spaces/dashes are stripped; check digit is validated (mod-10). Aliases: upc, ean, gtin, isbn, code.

**Returns:** valid, gtin_type, digits, gtin13, check_digit, expected_check_digit, issuing_country, is_isbn, reason (if invalid)

**Example request body:**
```json

}
```
